chapter: War years, Goodman and Woody Herman
title: Being a leader: headaches and judging new hires
summary: Asked about headaches, Norvo says problems come with leading, he listened to his men like a father-confessor and his mother said music cannot be played unhappily.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: As a leader did you -- did you have headaches, I mean headaches with the guys or --
No, I didn't have any headaches.
With -- you mean with the small band, you mean?

We worked -- we worked and they all enjoyed playing Specs had had experience, they all had experience, he'd been working in Cafe Society -- he worked there -- and I don't know he'd worked for Eddie South, over there on (inaudible) and he was a light drummer, he fitted perfect for that band.
He was a good drummer, wasn't he?
Yeah. It had a good feel. They were happy to play and they were exhuberant about playing.
Yeah, well when you were on the road with the big band, did you have headaches? Management headaches, or travelling --
Well no. What do you call headaches? It's like any business. When you have a business, do you have head-
-- you have problems, and why should it be any different with a band, it's a business, after all actually.
It may be a little different, but, actually when you're a leader, all the men's problems become your problems.

They don't know what to do. But you get so that when you hire people, for a band of that sort, they're with you for a couple of days, you know whether they're going to be people that can make the road or not make the road, you know immediately --
-- it's the way they handle themselves.
And you know who -- how they're going to be as musicians, by the way they fall into things.
That isn't such a mystery as it might seem. But headaches? I really didn't look at them as headaches, I just look at it as part of being a leader.
